method: Evidence pack from the release file; one Sonnet 5 agent established the facts and a second checked them independently; every quote verified against the release files and README; disputed fields corrected by hand; level and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
summary: When you choose One-click Deploy and confirm, it downloads the Skill-Runner backend (about 20 MB) from the developer's GitHub releases and runs it, then installs more software with uv. The file is checked only against a checksum from the same place.

facts.what: The Skill-Runner backend (a ~20 MB tar.gz from the developer's own Skill-Runner GitHub releases). The plugin unpacks it with tar, then runs its Python scripts through uv, which installs further engines on first setup.
facts.readmeQuote: The one-click local backend deployment is only suitable for users who cannot install Agent / Docker. Closing Zotero will terminate all tasks.

triggerQuote.text: No local backend info was detected. The plugin will download the backend release package and run automatic deployment. Continue?

facts.notes: Repo is leike0813/Skill-Runner (DEFAULT_SKILL_RUNNER_RELEASE_REPO), a different repo from the plugin's. The checksum is a .sha256 file fetched from the same GitHub release as the tarball, so it catches corruption but not a replaced release. The version tag comes from a runtime feed (resolveSkillRunnerRuntimeVersion) or a preference override. Release v0.7.9 asset is 20,590,739 bytes. Trigger is the 'One-click Deploy/Start' button in Preferences; a confirm dialog (confirmDeployForPlan) lists install paths and cancel aborts. Startup auto-ensure only restarts an already-deployed runtime. After extraction the plugin runs `uv run python scripts/agent_manager.py --ensure` (sh -lc, or powershell on Windows) with a 20 minute timeout. The README calls one-click deploy an emergency option and never says it downloads anything. I did not fetch the tarball or inspect what it contains. The plugin XPI is byte-identical in code to zotero-agents (same zotero-skills.js).

alsoAppliesTo.how: Same download code (release address, same-source checksum, confirmation prompt) as 0.8.4, compared by hand.
